vectors.description: An enforcing deployment-scoped quarantine. Every implementation verifies it and derives the same digest from the same bytes.
A structurally perfect lease signed by the routing-policy key. The signature verifies; the key was never provisioned to stop a runtime, so every implementation must refuse it.
A captured pre-quarantine lease replayed under the same leaseId. It is authentic, in window, and arrives last; it must not lift the live quarantine.
An advisory lease that names a quarantine and asks for staleAction stop, evaluated long after it expired. Mode is checked first, so this refuses no traffic anywhere.

An enforcing quarantine whose lease expired with staleAction continue. `continue` means keep enforcing what the last lease said, so the quarantine survives: otherwise it could be lifted by cutting the runtime off from the control plane.
An agent-scoped quarantine. The engine cannot resolve an agent identity, so it enforces nothing and must say so rather than show a green tick; the SDK host holds the identity and refuses work.

A genuine, correctly signed, unexpired `serving` lease carrying a different leaseId and a lower revision, replayed against a live quarantine. Revisions are ordered globally per (orgId, targetEnvironment), so changing the leaseId must not buy a replay past the guard.

An enforcing lease whose only matched control says `serving`, alongside a quarantine at a resolvable scope for somebody else. Both runtimes match a control and enforce nothing, so both report 0 and `advisory`.
lease-valid-v1 with one flipped signature bit.

acknowledgementVectors.description: The pinned shape from a replica refusing traffic for two matched quarantines while one control sits at a scope it cannot resolve.
A live lease under which this replica enforced nothing: §8c makes that `advisory` with a count of 0, and intake must store it as reported rather than inferring enforcement from the lease.

An expired lease under staleAction `continue`: the replica is still refusing, and says so. Intake must not read `stale` as `not enforcing` — that would make an unreachable issuer look like a lifted quarantine on the operator surface too.
A replica that has accepted no lease. It still declares the scopes it could resolve, because that describes the runtime and not the lease.
§5.11: a lease this replica could not read. It reports the failure and whatever it still holds; intake must record the failure rather than treating it as `no quarantine`.

§7b.18: unknown members inside the object are ignored. `mode` is one of them on purpose — it is the issuer's instruction, and a consumer that read it here would be reporting what the runtime was told instead of what it did.
§7b.18: an observation with no `runtimeControlAck` at all. This replica said nothing, which is not the same as reporting compliance and must never be counted as any.
`off` is not in the pinned enum (§7b.17). It is the value the pre-contract shape used, so accepting it here is how a stale producer goes unnoticed.
`enforcedControlCount` absent. A missing known member is fatal: defaulting it to 0 would silently rewrite what the replica said.
Enforcement claimed with no lease to enforce. §1: a surface may only claim enforcement it can prove, and this one cannot name what it is enforcing.
